name: SymbolIdentityResolve performance baseline (G14-01-POST-PERF-01)
scope: B-MINIMAL-FIX / PERF-01 — measurement only, no production code change
workload: 1 / 10 / 100 / 1000 resolves; both same id and distinct ids

analysis.perCallAverage: Same id: ~28us; Different ids: ~16us (different ids is FASTER because warm-path Roslyn cache skips duplicate GetSymbolsForDeclarationId invocations across the same compilation scan).
analysis.linearity: 100 -> 1000 is 6.5x (28.4 / 4.3) for same id; 7.9x (16.2 / 2.05) for different ids. Sub-linear. No GC pressure (gen0 = 0 across all 1000-resolve rows).
analysis.compilationSizeFactor: 40218 indexed records; Resolve per call is O(compilation-scan). 1000 distinct resolves = 16ms = 16us each.
analysis.practicalImpact: P14-02 reference resolution: a 1000-reference semantic model resolves in ~16ms. A 10000-reference model: ~160ms. Acceptable for compile-time work, no per-render pressure.

decision.summary: Performance is acceptable. No implementation change. Baseline recorded.

p14Perf01Backlog.rationale: Resolve's hot path is a single Roslyn API call; current measurements (16-28us / call, 0 GC) are within compile-time budgets. A Compilation-scoped index would add maintenance and lifecycle cost (per H8) for a sub-30us win. The Compile-once-Cache-forever pattern is owned by SnapshotReferenceCache (P13-H8) for the expression path; Resolve's id->symbol contract is read-mostly and small. Revisit if a 10x jump in indexed-record count or a per-render hot path is ever required.
revisitTriggers: Indexed record count > 200,000 AND any per-call hotspot in production traces
P14-02 Reference System needs per-render resolve (NOT compile-time)
P15 evolution requires resolving the same id more than 10x per compilation

exit: STOP — no code change authorized. G14-01-POST-PERF-01 PASS (baseline only).
